Laurence Sterne, The Life and Opinions of Tristram Shandy, Gentleman.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/laurence-sterne/the-life-and-opinions-of-tristram-shandy-gentleman

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Laurence Sterne, the author, died 1768 (Wikidata Q218960, P570 = 1768-03-18).
- George Saintsbury, the writer of the introduction, died 1933 (Wikidata Q1419967, P570 = 1933-01-28).

First publication of the text used: between 1759 and 1767. SE colophon: 'The Life and Opinions of Tristram Shandy, Gentleman was published between 1759 and 1767 by Laurence Sterne.'

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in between 1759 and 1767, before 1931, and the edition's rights statement (quoted below) places it in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin (not stated in the facts; the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa): each has a copyright term of life plus 70 years or less. The last person to die died in 1933, so the work is in the public domain in each of them no later than 1 January 2004.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
